pr.title: Spec a theme system for the panel
pr.head: ea28d6f84e6b55e9048000da62aee60b195d1200

summary: Projector's panel is the area Claude Code draws above the prompt. It lists the pull requests that the session's loops track and the inbox's questions and notices, and it colors each element by what the element means. Today every color is written into hooks/register.tsx where the element draws it, and only the background is a setting, panel.background, whose allowlist #341 merged.

This pull request adds one draft plan, docs/projects/panel-themes/readme.md, at priority later. It changes no code. The plan routes every color through thirteen named roles, such as muted, question, added, and removed. Each role defaults to the color it draws today, so the panel looks the same with no settings. A person overrides one role with panel.colors.<role>, picks a built-in theme with panel.theme, and keeps panel.background for the background. The panel reads the whole panel table in one project config get panel call, and it alone owns the role list and every check.

The later commits record the owner's decisions and answer the first review. The panel refuses a background that would hide the text Claude Code draws itself, which means white on a dark theme and black on a light one, so the plan partly reverses #341. watching and branch move from terminal palette slots to theme keys that the owner picks by preview. And the panel keeps a copy of Claude Code's theme values, so it can check a literal background against the defaults drawn on it, settling the background before the other roles.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Role: a named meaning, such as muted, that every element of that meaning draws in.
  • Theme key: a Claude Code color name, such as subtle, that resolves per theme. The public 23 are the ones the ThemeKey type lists.
  • Base: whether the Claude Code theme is dark or light, which picks the default background.
  • Layer: one source of a role's color: auto's defaults, then a built-in theme, then the person's own setting.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first review, of 7d13a5f, found that a literal background such as rgb(80,80,80) on dark hid the subtle header, hint, and ages with no toast. ea28d6f fixed it with a copy of Claude Code's theme values, and took all three suggestions.
  • The review of ea28d6f opened one finding: three edited lines run past the file's 75-column wrapping, which CLAUDE.md asks edits to match.
  • The plan is at draft, so its open questions don't block.

groups.title: The panel themes plan
groups.kicker: Thirteen color roles, three settings, a contrast check, and a three-step rollout
intro: The plan reads in order: the problem, the design in six parts, the reasons for it, the acceptance tests, the cost, the rollout, and the open questions. The design is what to check against the code, because each default claims to keep today's look.

Every claim about today's code held when the review checked it against main: the role table matches every color in hooks/register.tsx, the background table matches THEME_BACKGROUNDS, and the CLI reads and refuses the new keys as the plan says.

files.note: The new plan. Read § 2 for the design and § 2.5 for the contrast rules, which settle the background before the other roles.

checks.text: § 2.1: the role table matches every color and backgroundColor prop in hooks/register.tsx on main, checked prop by prop. No element uses dimColor.
Open finding: this line, and lines 177 and 239, run past the file's 75-column wrapping, which CLAUDE.md asks a Markdown edit to match.
§ 2.3: the literal colors and aliases match what #341 merged as BACKGROUND_ALIASES, HEX_COLOR, and NUMBERED_COLORS, and Claude Code's ThemeKey type lists exactly 23 keys.

§ 2.4: run in a scratch home, project config get panel --json prints null and exits 1 with no panel table, and prints the table merged across files otherwise. 0.7.20 behaves the same, and both refuse project config set panel.colors.muted with exit status 2.

§ 2.5: on dark, Claude Code 2.1.299 draws subtle as rgb(80,80,80), read from its theme data, so that background now falls back to rgb(20,20,20). Every other default that is a theme key stays at least 2.83:1 against it, so the row with a muted override draws both as set.

§ 7: on the ANSI themes and an unreadable custom theme, the panel still checks a literal background only against Claude Code's own text and exact matches, so a role's default can vanish there. The plan defers this until a plugin can read the terminal's palette.
